correctness.rationale: In odd characteristic the commutator is twice multiplication of the odd parts, so its rank subtracts from 64. For a nonzero linear part, the leading filtered maps from odd to even and even to odd each have rank at least 16 (wedge with the linear part), and the total rank is at most 32 since multiplication by an odd element squares to zero. With only a nonzero quintic the perfect degree-(1,5) pairing gives rank 1. With nonzero cubic and no linear part, the degree-four projection has rank 6-k, where k is the vector wedge-annihilator dimension, and the entire one-dimensional degree-six target is already hit by cubic inputs, so the quintic tail changes nothing. For a line in the annihilator the cubic factors by that line. A rank-two quotient bivector yields k=3; for the rank-four normal form e2∧e3+e4∧e5 the five quotient basis vectors give independent wedge images, hence k=1. The split cubic e1∧e2∧e3+e4∧e5∧e6 has k=0 by the two different bidegrees, so even the smallest odd field has all strata. Independently count line–cubic incidences as [6 choose 1]_q(q^10−1)=[3 choose 1]_q D+B. Counting the decomposable stratum by its unique support and the complement by subtraction, and restoring the independent degree-five and even components, gives the frozen table. The derivation handles nonprime fields as well; the symbolic checks are not the basis of that extension.
